source_text: Isti igitur impuri spiritus, daemones, ut ostensum a magis, a philosophis, et a Platone, sub statuis et imaginibus consecrati delitescunt, et afflatu suo auctoritatem, quasi praesentis numinis, consequuntur, dum inspirantur interim vatibus, dum fanis immorantur, dum nonnumquam extorum fibras animant, avium volatus gubernant, sortes regunt, oracula efficiunt falsis pluribus involuta. Nam et falluntur et fallunt, ut et nescientes sinceram veritatem, et quam sciunt, in perditionem sui non confitentes. Sic a coelo deorsum gravant, et a Deo vero ad materias avocant, vitam turbant, omnes inquietant, irrepentes etiam corporibus occulte, ut spiritus tenues, morbos fingunt, terrent mentes, membra distorquent, ut ad cultum sui cogant: ut nidore altarium, vel hostiis pecudum saginati remissis, quae constrinxerant curasse videantur. Hi sunt et furentes, quos in publicum videtis excurrere; vates et ipsi absque templo sic insaniunt, sic bacchantur, sic rotantur. Par et in illis instigatio daemonis, sed :ARGUMENTUM dispar furoris. De ipsis etiam illa quae paulo ante tibi dicta sunt, ut Jupiter ludos repeteret ex somnio, ut cum equis Castores viderentur, ut cingulum matronae navicula sequeretur. Haec omnia sciunt plerique pars vestrum, ipsos daemonas de semetipsis confiteri, quoties a nobis et tormentis verborum et orationis incendiis de corporibus exiguntur. Ipse Saturnus, et Serapis, et Jupiter, et quidquid daemonum colitis, victi dolore, quod sunt eloquuntur: nec utique in turpitudinem sui, nonnullis praesertim vestrum assistentibus, mentiuntur. Ipsis testibus, esse eos daemonas, de se verum confitentibus credite. Adjurati enim per Deum verum et solum, inviti miseris corporibus inhorrescunt: et vel exsiliunt statim, vel evanescunt gradatim, prout fides patientis adjuvat, aut gratia curantis aspirat. Sic Christianos de proximo fugitant, quos longe in coetibus per vos lacessebant. Ideo inserti mentibus imperitorum, odium nostri serunt occulte per timorem: naturale est enim et odisse, quem timeas; et quem metueris, infestare, si possis. Sic occupant animos, et obstruunt pectora, ut ante nos incipiant homines odisse, quam nosse: ne cognitos aut imitari possint, aut damnare non possint.
thought_title: Demons' Influence and Hatred Towards Christians
pass_a_gloss: These impure spirits, demons, as shown by magicians, philosophers, and Plato, lurk under statues and images consecrated, and by their breath gain authority, as if of a present divinity, while they inspire prophets, while they haunt temples, while they sometimes animate the fibers of entrails, govern the flights of birds, control lots, produce oracles involved in many falsehoods. For they both deceive and are deceived, so that they do not confess the true truth, which they know, to their own perdition. Thus they weigh down from heaven, and from the true God call away to material things, disturb life, disturb all, secretly penetrating even bodies, so that as thin spirits they create diseases, terrify minds, distort limbs, so that they may compel to their own worship: so that by the smell of altars, or by the sacrifices of animals, having been sated, they seem to have cured what they had bound. These are also the raving ones, whom you see rushing out in public; prophets also, without a temple, thus rave, thus become frenzied, thus spin around. Equal in them is the instigation of a demon, but the argument of fury is different. Also, about them, those things which a little while ago were said to you, that Jupiter would repeat games from a dream, that Castors would seem to be seen with horses, that a matron's girdle would follow a ship, all these things many of you know, that the demons themselves confess about themselves, as often as they are driven out from bodies by us, by the torments of words and the fires of prayer. Saturn himself, and Serapis, and Jupiter, and whatever demons you worship, conquered by pain, speak out what they are: nor indeed do they lie, especially with some of you present, to their own shame. Believe them, with them as witnesses, that they are demons, confessing the truth about themselves. For when adjured by the true and only God, they shudder, unwilling, in wretched bodies: and either they leap out immediately, or they gradually vanish, as the faith of the patient assists, or the grace of the healer inspires. Thus they hastily flee from the neighborhood of Christians, whom they had long been harassing in gatherings through you. Therefore, inserted in the minds of the unskilled, they secretly sow hatred of us through fear: for it is natural to hate him whom you fear, and to attack him whom you dread, if you can. Thus they occupy minds, and block hearts, so that men begin to hate us before they know us, so that they may not be able to know us, or imitate us, or not be able to condemn us.
pass_b_english: These impure spirits, demons, hide under statues and consecrated images, as magicians, philosophers, and Plato have shown. By their breath they seize authority, as if a divinity were present, while they inspire prophets, haunt temples, sometimes animate the fibers of entrails, govern the flights of birds, control lots, and produce oracles wrapped in many falsehoods. For they both deceive and are deceived, so that they do not confess the true truth they know, to their own perdition. Thus they weigh down from heaven and call people away from the true God to material things; they disturb life, disturb everyone, secretly penetrate even bodies, and as thin spirits they fabricate diseases, terrify minds, and distort limbs, so that they may compel worship of themselves: so that by the smell of altars, or by the sacrifices of fattened animals once sated, they may seem to have cured what they themselves had bound. These are also the raving ones you see rushing out in public; prophets, too, even without a temple, rave just so, frenzy just so, spin just so. The demonic instigation in them is equal, but the form of their madness differs. You also know those things I told you a little while ago about them: that Jupiter would renew games because of a dream, that the Castors would appear with horses, that a matron's girdle would follow a ship. Most of you know all this because the demons themselves confess it about themselves whenever we drive them out of bodies by the torments of words and the fires of prayer. Saturn himself, Serapis, Jupiter, and whatever demons you worship, conquered by pain, declare what they are; nor do they lie, especially with some of you present, to their own shame. Believe them as witnesses when they confess the truth about themselves: they are demons. For when adjured by the true and only God, they shudder unwillingly in wretched bodies, and either leap out immediately or fade away gradually, as the faith of the sufferer assists or the grace of the healer inspires. Thus they flee in haste from the neighborhood of Christians, whom they had long harassed in gatherings through you. Therefore, implanted in the minds of the unskilled, they secretly sow hatred of us through fear: for it is natural to hate those you fear, and to attack those you dread, if you can. Thus they occupy minds and block hearts, so that people begin to hate us before they know us, so that they cannot know us, nor imitate us, nor condemn us.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The translation of 'dispar furoris' as 'the argument of fury is different' (A) and 'the form of their madness differs' (B) both capture the sense of the distinction being made. The translation of 'imperitorum' as 'unskilled' (A) and 'unskilled' (B) is a potential point of tension (as 'imperitorum' usually refers to commanders), but since both Pass A and B agree on this specific rendering of the Latin, and the prompt requires checking A against B and the source, the internal consistency and adherence to the provided text are maintained.
